incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE to #eng-oncall: Observed sustained p99 latency spike on /v1/generate in prod (region: us-west-2). p95 ~1.2s -> 2.8s, p99 ~1.8s -> 6.3s starting 2026-03-14T09:07:00Z. Impact: streaming stalls and some user sessions hit 30s timeout.

alice (oncall): saw the page, I'm on it. grabbing Grafana now. any recent deploys?

bob (sre): no deploys in last 2 hours according to deploy-bot. rolling alerts show increase in queue depth on runtime-gpu-pool-3.

carlos (runtime): looking at per-shard logs: a subset of requests show extremely long KV cache lookups and repeated cache evictions. suspect fragmentation under high concurrent prefix reuse.

emma (ml-infra): uploading the quick queries I ran:
```
# p99 by model shard
sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"+Inf\",route=\"/v1/generate\"}[5m])) by (le,shard)
```
Chart: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency/kv-pressure (paste)

nisha (support): customers reporting streaming stalls in chat UIs, one reported reconnect required. flagged a customer SLA alert.

alice (oncall): ok immediate mitigations we can try: 1) temporarily reduce concurrency on impacted pool to cut eviction churn, 2) route heavy streaming traffic to fallback smaller-context model, 3) purge/compact cache on worst shards. opinions?

carlos (runtime): concur. also we can enable "kv-pin-hot-prefixes" which prevents eviction for popular prefixes and increase per-shard cache quota by +20% (risky). recommending staged approach: pin hot prefixes first.

bob (sre): I'm worried about prefill vs decode imbalance — telemetry shows prefill rate jumped 3x while decode workers saturated, causing long tail while waiting for token decode. that increases KV pressure since more prefixes get cached then evicted before decode reads.

emma (ml-infra): good point. we can throttle prefill rate immediately for streaming routes. config snippet to change:
```
# reduce prefill tokens per-request
runtime.config.streaming.prefill_rate_limit = 0.6  # from 1.0
```
I'll prepare the change and push to canary.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by emma: canary runtime-config (streaming.prefill_rate_limit=0.6) -> canary-group-2 at 2026-03-14T09:18:00Z

alice (oncall): bob, can you take shard-level compaction? command?

bob (sre): running compaction on shards 3,4,7 now. command: `./kvctl compact --shard=3,4,7 --mode=fast`

carlos (runtime): started pinning top prefixes for the last 10m hot-list on shard 3 and 4. pin list generated from top-k: `./kvctl top --shard=3 --k=200 > pinlist.txt` then `./kvctl pin --file=pinlist.txt`. will monitor eviction rates.

alice (oncall): routed 15% of traffic to fallback model `redwood-small-v2` for streaming endpoints to reduce decoding backlog. routing rule id: route-20260314-01.

nisha (support): updating impacted customer tickets: telling them we're throttling prefill and routing to fallback; ask them to report if stalls persist.

bob (sre): compaction completed on 3/4/7. eviction rate dropped by ~40% on those shards. p95 improved from 2.8s -> 1.6s within 6 minutes of compaction. p99 still elevated at ~3.2s but trending down.

emma (ml-infra): canary config applied and healthy. prefill rate reduced, decode worker cpu utilization dropped by ~30% on canary nodes. planning global rollout in 10m if stable.

carlos (runtime): pinning helped but revealed some badly fragmented segments — we need background defragmentation process to be run offline. scheduling follow-up issue.

alice (oncall): current status: mitigation in place: prefill throttle -> canary -> global, shard compaction done on hot shards, pin hot prefixes, 15% traffic to fallback model. customer impact reduced; still monitoring p99.

nisha (support): customers A, B, and C have been notified of mitigation; two customers asked for ETA on full fix.

bob (sre): short-term additional action: increase per-shard cache limit by +10% for shard 3 and 4 to reduce eviction churn until defrag job done. I'll open an infra change with rollback.

alice (oncall): agreed. please coordinate with change control and run small increase now.

deploy-bot: infra change submitted by bob: `cache_quota_increase(shard=[3,4],percent=10)` -> pending approval.

bob (sre): applied on shard 3 only (staged) and observed further decrease in p99 to ~2.2s. shard 4 pending.

carlos (runtime): note: logs show some requests still hitting double-lookup pattern where prefill inserted ephemeral prefixes that get evicted then decode re-requests them, doubling KV ops. we should add metric for double-lookup rate.

alice (oncall): good catch — bob can you add an alert for double-lookup rate > 0.5%?

bob (sre): done. alert rule: `sum(rate(kv_double_lookup_total[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) > 0.005`

emma (ml-infra): rolling global prefill throttle now. expect full rollout complete by 2026-03-14T09:35:00Z.

nisha (support): customers reporting UX improvements. giving thumbs up. :thumbsup:

alice (oncall): summary for handoff:
- Impact: p99 spike causing streaming stalls for some customers; time window 2026-03-14T09:07 - ongoing (mitigations in place).
- Root cause hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + eviction churn driven by prefill/ decode imbalance and spikes in concurrent prefix reuse.
- Mitigations applied: prefill rate throttle (canary->global), shard compaction on hot shards, pin hot prefixes, increase cache quota on shard 3, route 15% traffic to fallback model, added double-lookup alert.
- Next actions (post-handoff): schedule offline defragmentation job, instrument double-lookup metric and dashboards, consider redesign of prefill pipeline to avoid ephemeral prefix churn, postmortem and customer comms.

alice (oncall): handing off to bob for night shift. bob, you're oncall owner now — I'll update the incident channel and ops doc.

bob (sre): taking over. will watch p99 and double-lookup alert for next 4 hours. if we see re-regression, escalate and revert routing.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (partial); severity=sev2; owner=bob (sre); incident_id=INC-20260314-042.

alice (oncall): thx everyone. pulling myself out.

nisha (support): closing loop with customers: will send follow-up notice once defrag schedule is known.

carlos (runtime): opened tickets: RUNTIME-1892 (defrag job), RUNTIME-1893 (double-lookup instrumentation).

bob (sre): logging handoff in ops-runbook and marking incident for postmortem.

deploy-bot: canary -> global rollout completed for streaming.prefill_rate_limit at 2026-03-14T09:33:10Z: success.

alice (oncall): last check p99=1.9s, p95=1.3s, error rate normal. closing paging loop but keeping thread open for postmortem notes.
